findings.source_passage: The gurgling brook greeted us with its soft sounds, and the falling water glistened in the moonlight as its sparkling droplets splashed over the rocks.
findings.why_it_matters: This lyrical sentence establishes the sensory atmosphere of the clearing and provides a tonal contrast to the narrator's sardonic voice; its omission flattens the scene's mood transition.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the brook/waterfall description on arrival at the clearing, keeping the poetic register intact.

findings.source_passage: I picked up a stone and tossed it in the air to catch it in my palm. 'Here goes nothing. . .' I threw the stone.
findings.why_it_matters: The source's beat — toss, catch, pause, then throw — gives a distinct rhythmic hesitation that characterises the narrator's nervous bravado; the draft collapses it to a single flipped-stone gesture.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the two-beat action: toss-and-catch followed by a separate throw, preserving the comic-nervous pacing.

findings.source_passage: A grin slid onto my face as the water gurgled.
findings.why_it_matters: This small beat of satisfaction is a character-voice marker — the narrator's glee at being right about the trick — and its loss removes a layer of personality from the scene.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the narrator's grin/satisfaction beat after the column of water rises.

findings.source_passage: It wasn't easy being this close to such an ethereal being.
findings.source_locator: Paragraph 12, Miriam's internal note before 'Because he was hurt'
findings.why_it_matters: The narrator's wry self-aware aside about the Lady's overwhelming presence contributes to the distinctive deadpan-yet-sincere voice; without it the emotional confession that follows loses its ironic cushion.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the parenthetical note about the difficulty of standing close to the Lady before Miriam answers the saving question.

findings.source_passage: The clear water sparkled in the dim light of early morning.
findings.source_locator: After the Lady disappears, Miriam looks at the vial
findings.why_it_matters: The 'early morning' time-stamp is a small but concrete narrative detail that grounds the scene temporally; its absence removes a sense of the night having passed.
findings.suggested_fix: Include the 'dim light of early morning' detail when Miriam looks at the vial after the Lady vanishes.

findings.source_passage: The grave faces were paler, as was Xander.
findings.source_locator: Return to the castle, first sentence of that beat
findings.why_it_matters: The source makes the parallel explicit — faces paled, Xander paled — a small rhetorical mirror that the draft flattens into a vague 'faces had paled further.'
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the explicit parallel: grave faces paler, and Xander paler too.

summary: No high-severity signature losses; four medium-severity voice-flattening instances (sensory clearing description, stone-toss rhythm, narrator's grin beat, and the 'ethereal being' aside) and two low-severity omissions are present, falling below the three-medium regeneration threshold, so the draft passes but would benefit from restoring those narrator-voice beats.
